renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: evidence_dot_plot
  title: Evidence per caller and fusion
  description: |-
    Each dot is a fusion reported by one caller: its colour is the read support on a log scale and its size is the share of the fusion's total support that this caller holds. It answers which callers back each fusion and how strongly.
    How to read: a fusion with dots in several columns is found by several callers, which is the main reason to trust it. A fusion with a single dot rests on one caller. Compare colours within a caller, since callers count evidence differently.
    Lines and annotations: the colour scale is log10 of supporting reads plus 1, where the read count is normalised from each caller's own evidence fields by the recipe.
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: caller
    gene: fusion
    mean_expression: log_support
    frac_expressing: evidence_fraction

- component: figure
  title: Supporting reads per fusion
  description: |-
    Each bar stacks the callers of one fusion, with height their supporting reads and colour the caller. It answers which fusions have the most read evidence and which callers provide it.
    How to read: a tall bar made of several colours is a fusion with strong, shared support. A bar of one colour rests on one caller. Read counts are normalised from each caller's evidence fields, so compare callers with care.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fusion
    y: supporting_reads
    color: caller
    labels:
      fusion: Fusion
      supporting_reads: Supporting reads
      caller: Caller

- component: card
  title: Supporting reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median read support of a fusion as one caller reports it, with the lowest and highest beside it. It answers how strong the evidence is for a typical report.
    How to read: a very low median means thin evidence. The range is wide and callers count differently, so a box would draw a flat line.
  column: supporting_reads
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: vertical
  caption: median, lowest and highest

- component: card
  title: Fusions per caller
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct fusions, and the bars rank the callers by how many fusions each reports. It answers which caller finds the most.
    How to read: a caller far ahead of the others finds many fusions alone, which can mean sensitivity or noise. Compare with the agreement view.
  column: fusion
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fusions, by caller

- component: card
  title: Supporting reads by caller
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total read support over all reports, and the bars rank the callers by the support they contribute. It answers which caller carries the evidence.
    How to read: callers count evidence differently, so a larger total does not make a caller more accurate.
  column: supporting_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: supporting reads, by caller

- component: card
  title: Largest share held by one caller
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest share of a fusion's support held by one caller, between 0 and 1, and the histogram shows how shares are distributed over the reports. It answers whether support is spread across callers or concentrated in one.
    How to read: many shares near 1 mean fusions rest on one caller. A fusion reported by one caller always holds all of its support.
  column: evidence_fraction
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution across reports

- component: table
  title: Caller evidence table
  description: |-
    Each row is a fusion reported by one caller, with the breakpoints that caller gave, its supporting reads, its share of the fusion's support, the index and the caller's raw evidence string. It answers what each caller actually saw.
    How to read: filter on one fusion to compare its callers, and read the detail column for the caller's own fields.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: fusion

- component: advanced_viz
  id: caller_upset
  title: Caller agreement
  description: |-
    Each bar is a combination of callers and its height the number of fusions that exactly those callers reported, with the bars on the left giving each caller's total. It answers which callers agree on a fusion and which find calls alone.
    How to read: tall bars at high degree, where most callers agree, are the safest fusions to follow up. Fusions seen by one caller only are the most likely false positives, because the callers use different approaches. A caller with a large private bar adds sensitivity and noise in the same measure.
    Lines and annotations: bars are coloured by the number of callers in the combination, the degree of the intersection.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Clinical-Genomics/fusion-report/master/docs/score.md
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: advanced_viz
  id: fii_lollipop
  title: Fusions ranked by indication index
  description: |-
    Each lollipop is a fusion placed at its rank in fusion-report's ordering, coloured by how many callers found it and sized by its Fusion Indication Index. It answers which fusions fusion-report puts first and how many callers back them.
    How to read: the leftmost, large lollipops are the best candidates. A top-ranked fusion found by one caller only ranks high on database evidence alone, so look at the caller evidence tab before trusting it.
    Lines and annotations: the index is computed by fusion-report as 0.5 times the share of callers that found the fusion plus 0.5 times a weighted database score, with COSMIC and Mitelman weighted 50 each and FusionGDB2 0. It is a ranking score and not a probability.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Clinical-Genomics/fusion-report/master/docs/score.md
  kind: lollipop
  config:
    top_n_labels: 10
  roles:
    feature_id: fusion
    position: rank
    category: tool_support
    effect: fii
    label: fusion

- component: figure
  title: Fusion Indication Index per fusion
  description: |-
    Each bar is a fusion with its Fusion Indication Index, coloured by how many callers found it. It answers how strong the combined caller and database evidence is for each fusion.
    How to read: a high bar in the colour of several callers is a fusion both found by the tools and known to the databases. A short bar means few callers or no known database record.
    Lines and annotations: the index mixes caller agreement and database knowledge with equal weight, and database weights of COSMIC 50, Mitelman 50 and FusionGDB2 0.
     The dashed line is the median Fusion Indication Index of this table, a
    reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut- off of fusion-report.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Clinical-Genomics/fusion-report/master/docs/score.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fusion
    y: fii
    color: tool_support
    labels:
      fusion: Fusion
      fii: Fusion Indication Index
      tool_support: Callers
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: fii

- component: card
  title: Fusion Indication Index
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median Fusion Indication Index over the fusions in view, a score from 0 to 1, and the box shows the spread. It answers how well supported the fusions are as a set.
    How to read: a high median means most calls are backed by several callers or by databases. The index is fusion-report's own ranking score and is not a probability.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Clinical-Genomics/fusion-report/master/docs/score.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Clinical-Genomics/fusion-report/master/fusion_report/app.py
  column: fii
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Fusions reported
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct fusions, and the bars rank the caller agreement classes by how many fusions they hold. It answers how many fusions the callers report and how many several of them agree on.
    How to read: a large class of fusions found by one caller is the usual noisy part of a run. Follow up the classes with more callers first.
  column: fusion
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: tool_support
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fusions, by caller agreement
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Caller agreement composition
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of fusions and the ring splits them by how many callers found each. It answers what share of fusions have broad caller support.
    How to read: a big slice of single-caller fusions means a noisy run, and a big slice of many-caller fusions a well supported one. The second number is how many agreement levels appear.
  column: tool_support
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: tool_support
  caption: fusions, by caller agreement

- component: card
  title: Known to databases
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean count of fusion databases that already list a fusion, and the histogram shows its distribution. It answers how many of the calls are previously described.
    How to read: a fusion listed in several databases is known, a plus for a candidate. A fusion known to none may be novel or an artefact, and needs separate validation.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Clinical-Genomics/fusion-report/master/docs/score.md
  column: n_databases
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution across fusions

- component: table
  title: Fusion consensus table
  description: |-
    Each row is a fusion in one sample with its partner genes, the databases that know it, its Fusion Indication Index, the arithmetic behind it and a flag for each caller. It answers which fusions to validate and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by index or rank, then read the caller flags and the database list of the top calls.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: fusion
